brief: The Market Ear reads current flow and positioning data as unusually cautious given equity markets are near their highs. Morgan Stanley's Global Risk Demand Index has round-tripped back to neutral, Goldman's US Equity Sentiment Indicator has turned negative, US-domiciled equity fund inflows have collapsed, 20-day rolling ETF flows sit at multi-year lows, and JPMorgan flow data show modest re-grossing with slightly negative net flows and unchanged hedge fund leverage. Hedge funds also net sold equity macro products last week at the fastest pace since Liberation Day, and Goldman Prime data show gross long/short leverage down to the 20th percentile even as net leverage ticked up to the 6th percentile. The note's conclusion: broad FOMO is largely absent. The exceptions are hedge funds' net buying of US TMT stocks in 10 of the last 11 sessions, at the fastest pace since June 2025 (97th percentile, five-year lookback), and crypto funds' $6.8bn of inflows over six weeks. A closing aside flags CCC credit spreads creeping wider, still below 2022 wides.
